content: Typhoon Gaemi closed Kaohsiung port for 4 days in July 2024. Formosa Precision Capacitors (S01) shipments slipped 9 days in total because the port backlog took 5 extra days to clear after reopening. Lesson: for Kaohsiung closures, real delay is roughly closure length plus 5 days of backlog.

During the July 2024 Kaohsiung typhoon, Maya Chen approved air-freighting 40% of Formosa Precision Capacitors (S01) MLCC volume from Kaohsiung airport. It cost $180,000 in premium freight and fully avoided an Aurora router (AUR-1) line stoppage. Outcome: success; Maya said she would do it again.

In November 2024 Northwind bought MLCC capacitors from spot-market broker QuickChip Brokers during a shortage. 12% of the lot was counterfeit and caused a field recall of 3,000 Nimbus gateways costing $1.4M. Maya Chen banned spot-market brokers: never recommend brokers or grey-market sourcing.

Maya Chen's standing preference for risk briefs: lead with revenue at risk in USD, then list actions ranked by time-to-effect (fastest first), each with an estimated cost. Keep it under 250 words. She dislikes generic advice like 'monitor the situation' or 'diversify suppliers'.

Haiphong Circuit Works (S03) had a 6-day labor stoppage in March 2025 over overtime pay. Dual-sourcing to Bangalore Board Assembly (S10) worked but S10 needed 10 days to ramp to extra volume, so ramp requests must be placed on day one.

In June 2025 Penang MicroParts (S08) successfully ramped resistor supply by 3x within 2 weeks during a Brightline shortage. Penang MicroParts is Northwind's most responsive alternate for passives, and holds 30 days of consignment stock for Northwind that can be pulled with 48 hours notice.

Hurricane-related flooding in September 2025 shut the Laredo border crossing for 3 days. Monterrey Polymer Housings (S05) inventory buffer of 20 days absorbed it with no impact. Maya noted that 20-day buffers on enclosures mean short border closures can be ignored.

In October 2025 Maya Chen tried to qualify a second source for Wi-Fi radio modules because Shenzhen Everlight Modules (S04) is single-source for the Aurora router. Qualification takes 16 weeks and was not started due to budget. Single-source dependency on S04 remains Northwind's top structural risk.

Shenzhen Brightline Electronics (S07) failed a Northwind quality audit in March 2026: MLCC capacitance drift out of spec in 2 of 5 lots. A corrective action (CAPA-2291) is open. Do not shift volume to Brightline until the CAPA is closed.

In April 2026 Hsinchu Power Semiconductor (S06) warned that gallium export controls could cut its GaN wafer supply by 30%. Maya pre-bought 8 weeks of GaN power ICs, raising S06 inventory to 30 days. Northwind's contract with S06 includes an allocation-priority clause.

Northwind's logistics provider confirmed that Kaohsiung airport cargo capacity sells out within 24 hours of a typhoon warning. In a typhoon, air freight must be booked on the day the warning is issued, not after landfall.

Maya Chen prefers shifting IC substrate volume to Osaka Substrate Technologies (S09) over waiting on Kaohsiung Advanced Substrates (S02). S09 can absorb up to 25% extra volume with one week of notice, at a 6% unit-price premium.
